entries: Since 1974, Dungeons & Dragons has transformed the way people connect around the table. Today, it provides a creative lifeline to millions of gamers around the world, alongside community, laughs, tears, and triumphs. If food is here to nourish the body, then perhaps D&D is here to feed and sustain the imagination. It is no wonder that both dining and D&D so often find themselves at the center of our tables as hubs of community and connection.

In the original {@book Heroes' Feast: The Official D&D Cookbook|HF}, we explored how in-world food could elevate the gaming experience, organizing the book around the game's most iconic species and the cuisine they are known for. In the sequel, {@book Heroes' Feast: Flavors of the Multiverse|HFFotM}, we were even more ambitious, suggesting D&D food not only enhance your weekly game but also become a centering and essential part of it. In that installment, a group of madcap adventurers dined their way across the multiverse, feasting upon the finest fare of each realm while reminding us of the remarkable range of delicious flavors in our own.

Now, we have proudly cooked up another essential tool for integrating food into your D&D campaigns, your D&D campaigns into your food, and daily life beyond it. In {@book Heroes' Feast: Legends of the Table|HFLotT}, we explore the unique cuisine and foodways of each playable class, from their preferred ingredients and preparations to dining habits and presentation. Would a wizard who devotes themselves to the secrets of arcane magic prepare rothé the same way as a ranger who lives off the land? Might the tastes of a cloistered monk differ from those of the barbarian who lives on the frozen tundra? Can an on-the-run rogue or starving bard afford to be choosy with their diets? Perhaps most important, what in the world manifests when a cleric casts {@spell Create Food and Water|XPHB}? These, and many others, are the questions that inspired this ambitious quest and the eighty recipes that follow.

Just like the game that inspired it, the Heroes' Feast series is here to help you connect with others even while stoking your own creativity in the most delicious way imaginable. But if there's one thing Dungeons & Dragons has taught us, it's that the rules are just a starting point. They're a framework, not a finish line. In D&D, we customize. We homebrew. We take what's written and make it our own. The same spirit belongs in the kitchen.

So, break the rules. Or bend them. Or ignore them entirely. Recipes aren't commandments; they're invitations. Tinker like an artificer, improvise like a bard, forage like a druid, and season like a fighter with something to prove. Add your own regional flair. Combine flavors no diviner wizard saw coming. And above all, share what you make. Just like a good campaign, meals are meant to be remembered together.
To you and to your friends, families, and party members, we leave you with this blessing from the original {@i Player's Handbook}: "Enjoy, and may the dice be good to you."

entries.name: About This Book: A Feast of Class
entries: Every adventurer brings something unique to the party—and to the plate. In the worlds of Dungeons & Dragons, your class defines your strengths, your spells, your skills, and even your appetites. This unique cookbook explores the cuisine of the classes: Dishes inspired by the lives, traditions, and travels of wizards, fighters, rogues, druids, barbarians, and more.

Some recipes are culled from the menus of legendary inns and fabled strongholds. Others are rustic meals foraged in the wild or ancient delicacies passed down through monasteries, thieves' guilds, and magical colleges. A ranger's stew tastes of campfire smoke and forest herbs, while a bard's feast is spiced with flair and flair alone. A paladin's roast carries the sacred flavor of discipline; a warlock's dessert...well, it may cost more than it appears.

The good news is you won't need a spellbook or divine favor to make any of these recipes. We've swapped out rare planar ingredients for real-world substitutes—so, casting {@spell plane shift|XPHB} will not be required. Our culinary team has tested each dish with care, adapting fantasy into something flavorful, accessible, and most importantly, table ready.

Whether you're a seasoned chef or a culinary cantrip-caster, these recipes are designed to be both practical and transportive. They are also organized to help you explore the heart of each class's culture while making sure you don't trip any traps along the way.

As always, we've included headnotes for added lore to help connect the stories of these recipes with the storytelling in your game. You'll also find "Cook's Notes" for additional insights, useful whether you're sautéing at home or preparing a critical hit at your next game night.

entries.name: Tools Proficiencies Required
entries: No dungeon delver ventures forth without a backpack and a torch. And no chef should either (figuratively speaking). While not every dish in this book requires specialized tools, here are some essentials that will help ensure your success and perhaps even unlock a few bonus proficiencies along the way:

items: Measuring cups and spoons (precision is a wizard's ally)
Mortar and pestle (a must-have for druids and potion-makers)
Pie plate and loaf pans (even the lonely sorcerer craves dessert)
Garlic press (to keep the vampires away)
French press or coffee gear (trust us: bards need it)
Cocktail shaker and muddler (we are all alchemists at heart)

entries: From forging a holiday feast to prepping trail rations for your next foray into the wilderness, the right gear—and the right recipe—makes all the difference.

entries.name: Worlds of Flavor
entries: Dungeons & Dragons spans numerous campaign settings, each rooted in a unique world with its own history, mythology, culture...and cuisine. This cookbook explores several of these iconic realms but centers its lens on the culinary traditions of the adventuring classes who call them home—including fighters, wizards, rogues, clerics, and more—each bringing their own flavors to the world's table. Though originally designed for adventure and storytelling, each setting also offers distinctive ingredients, traditions, and techniques that invite culinary discovery. These locales include...

entries.name: Forgotten Realms
entries: The Forgotten Realms is a cornerstone of Dungeons & Dragons, an expansive world shaped by myth, magic, and centuries of storytelling. Created by Ed Greenwood, the setting unfolds across the planet Toril, whose continents include Kara-Tur, Maztica, Zakhara, and the widely explored Faerûn. Beneath it all lies the Underdark, a vast subterranean network teeming with danger and mystery. Faerûn is home to some of the game's most iconic regions and cities: the Sword Coast, Calimshan, Cormyr, Icewind Dale, Thay, and famed ports like Baldur's Gate, Neverwinter, and Waterdeep. The culinary traditions of Toril reflect its cultural breadth, ranging from hearty fare inspired by medieval Europe to vibrant dishes influenced by Asian and Indigenous American cuisines. These foodways evolve not only through the land's diverse peoples but also through the adventurers who reside there.

entries.name: Dragonlance
entries: Born from the imaginations of Tracy Hickman and Margaret Weis, Dragonlance presents a soaring vision of high fantasy—a world of misty woodlands, crystal lakes, snowcapped mountains, and dragons that fill the skies. But beneath its beauty lies constant turmoil. The planet Krynn is shaped by conflict: between gods and mortals, dragons and humanoids, balance and ambition. Magic is scarce, and survival often depends on courage, faith, and the strength of unlikely alliances. The continent of Ansalon, Krynn's most explored landmass, is the backdrop for many of the setting's most notable tales, from the gleaming towers of Istar to the treetop homes of Solace, the strongholds of Solamnia, and the haunted ruins of Xak Tsaroth. The food of Krynn mirrors its diversity: rustic tavern stews, elven delicacies from the forests of Silvanesti, and bold flavors inspired by Eastern traditions, all woven into the daily life of adventurers and common folk alike.

entries.name: Spelljammer
entries: Conceived by Jeff Grubb, Spelljammer launched Dungeons & Dragons beyond traditional fantasy realms and into the cosmos. An audacious blend of swashbuckling adventure and spacefaring wonder, it introduced magical ships—spelljammers—that sail the Astral Sea, linking distant worlds and allowing characters to journey between settings once thought separate. This imaginative leap not only expanded the scope of gameplay but opened a gateway to boundless celestial destinations, wild new adversaries, and colorful interplanetary intrigue. Exotic ports like the Rock of Bral, a bustling planetoid orbiting Toril, capture the setting's heightened space opera flair. In the expanse of Spelljammer, cultures collide, and cuisine evolves into something utterly unique, where the next meal might come from a forgotten moon or a traveling tavern crewed by autognome gastronomes.

entries.name: Greyhawk
entries: Greyhawk is the original campaign setting of Dungeons & Dragons, envisioned by co-creator Gary Gygax as a grounded world of perilous dungeons, arcane secrets, and medieval intrigue. Set on the planet Oerth, a land shaped by oceans, continents, and feuding powers, its most storied region is the Flanaess, a cultural crossroads dotted with legendary cities and perilous wilds. Kingdoms like Keoland, Veluna, the Shield Lands, and Furyondy stand alongside storied sites such as the Free City of Greyhawk, White Plume Mountain, the Village of Hommlet, and Blackmoor. Magic exists here, but it is often feared, regulated, or forbidden, lurking in tombs, towers, and war-torn borders. The setting's sensibilities draw heavily from feudal Europe, especially Britain, imbuing the cuisine with rustic charm: trenchers filled with stew, fire-roasted meats, and ale-battered fare meant to fortify adventurers before the next delve. With its earthy tone and emphasis on mortal struggle, Greyhawk remains a foundational setting, one where survival is hard-earned, and comfort can be found in the glow of a campfire.

entries.name: Eberron
entries: Eberron is a war-scarred world powered by innovation, prophecy, and intrigue, where magic meets machinery. Conceived by Keith Baker, the setting reimagines high fantasy through a pulp-infused, steampunk lens: Airships drift between cities, sentient constructs walk among mortals, and arcane energy fuels everything from streetlamps to lightning rails. At the heart of it all lies the continent of Khorvaire, once united under the Kingdom of Galifar and now fractured into the Five Nations: Aundair, Breland, Karrnath, Thrane, and the devastated Mournland. These differences are reflected in Eberron's cuisine, which is as daring as it is refined. In Sharn, sky-high kitchens fuse charm and alchemy. In Karrnath, bold, hearty meals sustain a nation hardened by war. Eberron's cuisine spans from humble field fare to enchanted, gear-crafted delicacies, all yielding flavors as bold and unconventional as the adventurers who call this world home.

entries.name: Planescape
entries: At the crossroads of belief and reality lies Sigil, an ever-shifting city perched atop the Spire at the center of the Great Wheel. Suspended on the inner curve of a floating torus, this "City of Doors" connects to every plane through countless portals. Designed by David "Zeb" Cook, the Planescape setting granted D&D a home for its most surreal and far-reaching ideas. First hinted at in Jeff Grubb's {@i Manual of the Planes} (1987), the Spire and Outlands came fully to life seven years later, offering players a world where factions clash over ideology and belief alone can reshape existence. In Sigil, contradiction is law: Gods are barred, yet street prophets alter reality through sheer conviction. Buildings spiral skyward only to vanish into shadowed alleys. Cultures collide, mix, and mutate. This tension extends to its food, where flavors are born of barter and belief. No two meals in Sigil are ever the same...and no appetite returns unchanged.

entries.name: Plane Food
entries: The Dungeons & Dragons multiverse spans more than just worlds; it unfolds across an intricate web of planes—entire dimensions layered around the Prime Material Plane, the baseline "reality" countless adventurers call home. Some of these planes are echo-like reflections, tethered closely to the Material Plane. Others stretch far beyond, homes to deities, devils, and dreamscapes. Each realm, no matter how arcane, carries its own customs and, of course, cuisine.

entries.name: The Feywild
entries: Also known as the Plane of Faerie, the Feywild is a luminous mirror of the Material Plane, aglow with eternal twilight and lush with fantastical flora. It is a realm of magic unbound rife with passion, mischief, and emotional extremes. Fey creatures, {@race harengon|MPMM} (rabbit folk), and ancient spirits call it home. Here, every sense is heightened—colors more vivid, music more stirring, and food more intense. In the Feywild, a meal is never just sustenance; it is a story, a temptation, or a trap.

entries.name: The Shadowfell
entries: The Shadowfell is the Feywild's bleak twin: a grayscale echo of the Material Plane, steeped in despair. This land of silence and decay houses the undead, the forgotten, and the cursed. Hope does not flourish here, and neither does flavor. Food here is bland and joyless, a pale imitation of what it once was. Among the mist-shrouded ruins lurk the Domains of Dread, self-contained demiplanes ruled by dark lords, where fear takes physical form and escape is all but impossible. Whatever food is harvested here is as colorless and drained as the realm itself.

entries.name: Ravenloft
entries: The most infamous of the Domains of Dread, Ravenloft centers on the haunted land of Barovia and its vampiric overlord, Count {@creature Strahd von Zarovich|RHW}. Conceived in 1983 by Tracy and Laura Hickman, Ravenloft has become a legend in its own right—a gothic nightmare enshrouded in fog and tragedy. Accessible only through the Shadowfell (and often unwillingly), its dreary atmosphere clings to everything: the architecture, the weather, and the food. Meals are heavy, often blood-tinged or brined, and best eaten with one eye on the door. In Barovia, every dinner could be your last.

entries.name: Beyond
entries: The culinary adventure doesn't end with the worlds detailed in these pages. The greater Dungeons & Dragons multiverse stretches endlessly outward, encompassing realms as wild and wondrous as imagination allows. There's Athas, the sun-blasted world of Dark Sun, where magic drains the land itself and food is forged from grit and survival alone. There's Strixhaven, the interplanar university where magical disciplines are matched only by cafeteria innovation, and even the desserts are enchanted. From the towering guildhalls and floating spires of Ravnica, where food follows function and faction, to the Radiant Citadel, a sanctuary of cultures from across the Ethereal Plane, the worlds of D&D remain as vibrant and varied as the people who play within them. Each realm offers its own tastes, traditions, and table, and although we can't visit them all here, their flavors echo through every feast born of adventure.

entries.by: Heafstaag, King of The Tribe of the Elk

entries: Across the known worlds, barbarians are fierce warriors shaped by the unforgiving lands they call home. While a lone barbarian is formidable, a clan in full fury is a force of nature. {@class Barbarian|XPHB|Barbarians} walk several different paths that imbue their lives with deeper meaning. From the {@subclass Berserker|Barbarian|XPHB|XPHB|Berserker's} adherence to raw violence to the {@subclass Wild Heart|Barbarian|XPHB|XPHB|Wild Heart's} ability to manifest kinship with animals, or the {@subclass World Tree|Barbarian|XPHB|XPHB|World Tree's} unique ability to tap into cosmic vitality to the {@subclass Zealot|Barbarian|XPHB|XPHB|Zealot's} union with their god while raging—these paths shape their worldview. In all cases, rage is the power that enhances their senses and makes them adept in battle.

{@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1|XPHB} is a deeply personal concept to the barbarian, and each interprets it differently. Some view it as a primal connection to the suffering of the world—an uncontrolled expression of wild magic. Others personify their rage as a revered ancestor or wild spirit or even as the true manifestation of their deepest selves. Yet beyond rage and battle, these wild folk are rooted in rich traditions centered on food, drink, and celebration.

entries.name: Feast, Fire, and Fury
entries: From the frosty tundra of Faerûn to the primal frontiers of Khorvaire and windswept steppes of Krynn, barbarian cultures live in close harmony with the land. Known to be fueled by their rage, barbarians carry this same zeal into all aspects of their foodways, from hunting and foraging to preparation and feasting. Food is never just sustenance; it's a primal expression of identity.

For the barbarian, feasting by fire is a shared tradition. From Icewind Dale to Droaam, the communal meal is sacred; it is a time to celebrate kinship, honor spirits, and give thanks for survival. These gatherings mark seasonal shifts, spiritual trials, and the strengthening of bonds between people and the wild. Across the great expanse of worlds, food and drink serve as sacrosanct rites, marking thresholds of transformation and communion with the forces that shape them. A young warrior might consume the heart of their first kill; a tribal leader may fast for days before imbibing {@recipe Jhuild|HFLotT} to gain clarity. In some clans, only those who endure Fire Root Stew are deemed strong enough to join the warband.

entries.name: Many Worlds, One Flame
entries: Though the barbarian tribes of the multiverse span wildly different realms, their cultures are bound by powerful ties.

On Toril, barbarian tribes roam Faerûn's frontiers, from the Silver Marches and Icewind Dale to the Great Glacier. Among the Reghedmen of the north, a proud, nomadic people living beyond the Spine of the World, meat is a staple: Boar, elk, reindeer, seal, and snowshoe hare are hunted and preserved by smoking or freezing. Glacier Jerky, salted elk or yeti meat frozen into chewable rations, offers portable proteins for their high-energy lifestyle. Raw fish, pine nuts, lichen, fermented vegetables in seal fat, and whale blubber provide vital winter nutrients. These well-organized tribes live in tented encampments and cook over fire. Hoarding is taboo, and hunters provide for all, often in honor of {@deity Auril|Faerûnian|FRHoF|Auril, the Frostmaiden}. Reghedmen celebrations follow the rhythm of the seasons, marked by multiday feasts. For example, the Feast of Sun's Return, heralding spring's first sun, is celebrated with sun effigies burned in bonfires and communal platters of hearty dishes such as Reghed Venison Pot Roast.

To the south, the nomadic Uthgardt roam the Savage Frontier. Known for aggression, these totem-worshippers perform meat-rich rituals to commune with ancestral spirits. Children of the open plains who are skilled in pit cooking, they survive on bison or Rothé Steaks, accompanied by root vegetables, wild grains, horse milk, honey, and Ashbread, a flatbread baked in embers with wild herbs.

Near Toril's equator, barbarian cultures flourish in a vastly different ecosystem: The lush, perilous jungles of the Chultan Peninsula and its tropical neighbors. Amid rainforests teeming with predators, their cuisine includes snake, insects, fish, yams, cassava, coconut, firefruit, and dinosaur meat. Cooking methods like volcanic rock grilling and banana-leaf steaming reflect an intimate knowledge of the land.

On the war-torn planet Krynn, the Ice Barbarians, Plainsfolk, and Khalkist Nomads uphold spiritual traditions shaped by gods and elemental forces. In the frozen north, the Ice Folk treat feasting as sacred. Their diet consisting of seal fat, dried kelp, snow berries, and wind-whale blubber requires little cooking. Varkaan, a sacred brew of snowmelt, powdered bone, fermented lichen, and moonspice, is reserved for warrior rites and funerals.

Across the Abanasinian Steppe, the Plainsfolk favor simple but meaningful meals. Their festivals honor spirits and mark the return of lost souls, blending food, fire, and oral tradition. Clan gatherings feature roasted game, corn cakes, berry jams, and tallow-fried breads, washed down with Sunmilk, a fermented goat's milk sweetened with blossom syrup. Effigies of sorrow are burned, and ancestral tales dating before the Cataclysm are chanted by firelight.

In the rugged Khalkist Mountains, the Khalkist Nomads herd goats and sheep for milk, meat, and cheese. Expert hunters and foragers, they subsist on wild game, hoppers (rabbits), sky-singers (birds), and alpine herbs. Mobility is key, so they rely on cured meats and hard cheeses that endure long journeys. Their humble but hearty feasts center on rich, travel-ready stews and open-fire feasts such as {@recipe Seared Boar and Potatoes|HFLotT}.

On Eberron, barbarian clans roam the planet's vast wilderness. These powerful peoples share a deep spiritual bond with primal forces, druidic sects, and the elemental planes. Most tribes hail from the Eldeen Reaches, the Shadow Marches, or the wilds of Droaam. Eberron's barbarians are seasoned warriors who live in harmony with their environment.

Within the Shadow Marches, skilled barbarian chefs prepare meals over greenflame, fires infused with primal magic. Around council fires, they share pots of Blackroot Stew and mugs of Thar'kaal, a glowing drink made from ghostbulb fungus, said to invite ancestral spirits.

In the Eldeen Reaches of Western Khorvaire, dense forests shelter barbarian tribes, many of them shifters, long descendants of lycanthropes who embrace their primal nature. To them, food is a blessing from the land. During midsummer Moonrise Hunt, tribes hunt enchanted forests, culminating in a moonlit feast where shamans chant tales and summon totemic spirits with drumming and dancing.

Far to the east, on the Dragon-continent of Argonnessen, the Dragonbone Reavers reign. Their feasts fuel both battles and dreams, and whether gnawing on Smoked Wolf Thigh or sipping Fermented Mushroom Brew beneath the stars, every bite reflects their fierce and extreme way of life.

entries.name: The Clan Eternal
entries: Untamed by planet or environment, the barbarian spirit roams free. Their feasts are rituals of meaning, their drinks anointed with the power of the divine, and their festivals anchored in cycles older than empires. More than mere berserkers, the barbarians are the keepers of story, guardians of tradition, and living links to the wild forces that shape their worlds.

entries: {@class Bard|XPHB|Bards} are the true artists and entertainers of the multiverse. They use their natural charms and talents as performers alongside their penchant for illusory magic to lighten moods, frighten enemies, and even inspire allies in battle. Sometimes called a "{@classFeature jack of all trades|Bard|XPHB|2|XPHB}," the bard dabbles in a little of everything from magic and swordplay to storytelling, song, and dance. Most are fueled by the belief that the multiverse was spoken into being by "{@classFeature Words of Creation|Bard|XPHB|20|XPHB}," and they carry that tradition forward through the inspired creations of their own, from performance and poetry to the food that they prepare and consume. Of course, any good bard will insist that their cooking is every bit as inspired as the very words they speak and sing.

entries.name: Jack of All Trades
entries: The talents of the bard are as broad and diverse as the multiverse they inhabit. Most belong to a loose association of mentors and peers known as a "college," which aligns with their beliefs and even helps them define and hone their talents. These affiliations not only inspire their artistic creations but equally influence their culinary tastes and gifts. For example, a bard who adheres to the {@subclass Creation|Bard|XPHB|TCE|College of Creation} and celebrates the cosmos as a work of art might favor clean, natural flavors and ingredients, while a bard of the {@subclass Eloquence|Bard|XPHB|TCE|College of Eloquence} might prefer highly complex gastronomic creations worthy of the sophisticated wordplay and rhetoric they espouse. With those who are rooted in the {@subclass Glamour|Bard|XPHB|XPHB|College of Glamour}, presentation is paramount as they create foods meant as much to feed the eyes as the belly, while those who follow the {@subclass Lore|Bard|XPHB|XPHB|College of Lore} view every ingredient and dish as an opportunity to tell a story. Curious what's in the {@recipe Sword Coast Seafood Bouillabaisse|HF|Sword Coast Bouillabaisse}? Grab a flagon of {@recipe Sweet Butter Ale|HFLotT}, sit back, and get ready for a tale.

When it comes to the preparation of fine cuisine, it is often bards of the {@subclass Swords|Bard|XPHB|XGE|College of Swords} who use their exceptional skill with the blade to butcher and prepare the best cuts of meat. Meanwhile, those who come from the {@subclass Valor|Bard|XPHB|XPHB|College of Valor} carry their obsession with bravery into their culinary concoctions, which can lead to exquisite flavor combinations or, just as often, dismal culinary failures. In all cases, the bard's focus and expertise with arcane magic is useful in their ability to not only follow and create complex recipes but also aid in food preparation through spells like {@spell mage hand|XPHB} and {@spell prestidigitation|XPHB}.

entries.name: Inspired Ingredients
entries: Bards of the multiverse are nothing if not resourceful. Whether it be circumstances or ingredients, the scrappy bard will always find a way to make the best out of any situation—or make lemonade out of lemons, as they say in Amn. It follows then that the preferred pantry of the bard is anything they run across that might add a bit of interest or drama to their food. A random encounter with vallenwood root along the trails of Ansalon or a rare fire spice from the markets of Sigil might lead to an inspired dish worthy of song.

However, for a bard to be fulfilled, they usually need to be where the audiences are, such as taverns, eating houses, public squares, and marketplaces. That means the general fare of the bard is geared to the broadest palates, favoring the foods of taverns, inns, and street vendors. Common root vegetables, grains, fish, poultry, beef, and {@creature rothé|VGM} are typical ingredients for the traveling eclectic but are always prepared with a bit of flourish and flair. Bards are also masters of atmosphere, so they recognize any dish can be enhanced with the right aesthetic, music, or conversation. The goal is not merely flavor, but rather to deliver an overall culinary experience that the diner won't soon forget.

entries.name: The Multiversal Language
entries: Music has often been described as the multiversal language, but many believe that food is more deserving of the moniker. Whatever the case, bards recognize that both can unite, inspire, and stir people's souls wherever their travels may take them, which includes virtually every corner of the multiverse.

On Toril, many bards can be found wandering the northern parts of Faerûn and the Dalelands, searching for adventure, wealth, love, or simply a willing audience to entertain. They often find tasty ingredients and spices along the way, sampling the best the world has to offer, from the {@recipe Traveler's Stew|HF} of the Yawning Portal to the {@recipe Cherrybread|HF} of the Elfsong Tavern in Baldur's Gate. Known as forever optimists and hopeless romantics, many Faerûnian bards find themselves inspired to use their talents for a greater purpose, serving virtuous and secretive organizations such as the Harpers, or their insidious and clandestine counterparts, the Zhentarim.

Bards who roam the reaches of Abanasinia on Krynn are bound to happen upon some of the greatest tavern-fare across the multiverse. Legendary establishments such as the Inn of the Last Home serve up inspiring food and drink like mouthwatering {@recipe Tavern "Steak"|HF|Tavern Steaks} and {@recipe Tika's Honey Mead|HFFotM|Tika's famous Honey Mead} even as bards earn their dinner by regaling guests with stories by the hearth. Those who make their way to the northern reaches of Solamnia to the City of Kalaman will delight in {@recipe Tamarind Balls|HFFotM} found in the bazaars or fresh {@recipe Steak of the Deep|HFFotM} on offer at the Sea Steed tavern.

In the City of Greyhawk, on the world of Oerth, shadowy bards of the {@subclass Whispers|Bard|XPHB|XGE|College of Whispers} can be found skulking in corners of the Green Dragon Inn supping on {@recipe Chocolate Scones with Yak Butter|HFLotT} while eavesdropping on the hushed conversations of adjacent booths. More restless bards might be spied roaming the world's country hamlets preparing a roadside Hommlet Omelet made from fresh goose, duck, or quail eggs.

entries.name: Foods of Inspiration
entries: No matter where their travels take them, bards will always surround themselves with food that is more than meets the eye. As cooks, they will scrounge up a scrappy celebration of flavors, illusions, and distractions that make for an unforgettable dining experience. As diners, their tastes necessarily follow their travels, which is anywhere a gracious audience can be found.

data.name: Cleric

entries: If any is the pet, I fear it is I. Percival accepts my friendship—sometimes—and my food—rather eagerly.

{@class Cleric|XPHB|Clerics} are the divine stewards of the multiverse, charged not only to serve their gods but to nourish the bodies and spirits of those around them. Whether tending to the sick, guiding the faithful, or standing firm in the face of cosmic evil, clerics channel divine energy into the world and often into their kitchens. For many clerics, the act of preparing food is an extension of their sacred rites: a ritual of hospitality, healing, and humble devotion.

entries.name: Divine Purpose
entries: Cleric domains channel the countless expressions of the gods' will, each one reflecting a distinct facet of the divine—wrath and mercy, light and shadow, war and wisdom. {@subclass Life|Cleric|XPHB|XPHB|Life Domain} clerics are living embodiments of restoration and care, while {@subclass War|Cleric|XPHB|XPHB|War Domain} clerics stride boldly into conflict, bolstering allies with righteous fury. {@subclass Light|Cleric|XPHB|XPHB|Light Domain} clerics act as beacons against darkness, wielding radiance as both shield and judgment, whereas {@subclass Grave|Cleric|XPHB|RHW|Grave Domain} clerics traverse the shadowed edge between death and peace. {@subclass Trickery|Cleric|XPHB|XPHB|Trickery Domain} clerics delight in subversion and sacred mischief, while {@subclass Knowledge|Cleric|XPHB|FRHoF|Knowledge Domain} clerics preserve the lore of the cosmos itself. Even within the same pantheon, two clerics may differ wildly in outlook and method, each channeling the divine through their chosen creed. But regardless of their domain, clerics bring unwavering dedication and focus to the table.

entries.name: Sacred Sustenance
entries: Where wizards measure grams and glyphs, clerics measure compassion. Their food is rarely about flair; it's about meaning. Meals prepared by a cleric often carry symbolic weight, draw from ancient temple traditions, or serve as a vehicle for blessings. In the hands of a cleric, a loaf of bread is more than sustenance—it's an offering, a ward, or even a vessel for divine magic.

Clerics of healing deities such as {@deity Ilmater|Faerûnian|FRHoF} or {@deity Eldath|Faerûnian|FRHoF} often brew restorative broths rich in garlic, bone, and curative herbs, passed down through temple kitchens for centuries. Worshippers of {@deity Chauntea|Faerûnian|FRHoF}, the Grain Goddess, might create multigrain harvest loaves blessed to stay fresh for weeks. Followers of {@deity Moradin|Dwarven|SCAG}, the dwarven "All-Father" who embodies the unbreakable spirit of dwarvenkind, craft hearty meals meant to strengthen the body for labor and forgework, often accompanied by a strong dwarven ale.

Some clerics imbue their cooking with divine magic courtesy of low-level spells like {@spell purify food and drink|XPHB} or {@spell ceremony|XGE}, which bestow benefits of cleansing or healing benefits. Similarly, the effects of a {@spell lesser restoration|XPHB} or {@spell remove curse|XPHB} spell might be delivered via food. And where no nourishment exists at all, a skilled cleric can conjure it forth via {@spell create food and water|XPHB} in a quantity to feed a small village. {@spell Heroes' feast|XPHB}, a more advanced cleric casting, offers powerful resistances, immunities, and other boosts on the eve of battle to twelve fortunate partakers. Despite their varied invocations, clerics often initiate the joy of sharing a meal with those in need, an act of service that is, in many faiths, its own form of prayer.

entries.name: Feasts of Faith
entries: Clerics' culinary traditions vary widely depending on their pantheon and plane of origin. In Faerûn, temples commonly operate public kitchens as part of their divine charge. In Baldur's Gate on feast days, devotees of {@deity Tymora|Faerûnian|FRHoF} serve Blessed Luck-Cakes, which are coin-shaped pastries filled with dates and honey that supposedly bestow a day's good fortune. In Waterdeep, faithful priests of {@deity Sune|Faerûnian|FRHoF} serve celebratory {@recipe Wedding Soup|HFLotT} after performing the sacred nuptials. In the cloistered chapterhouses of {@deity Oghma|Faerûnian|FRHoF}, the Binder of Knowledge, clerics craft Scroll Soup, which has noodles inscribed with prayers in edible ink and is consumed in reverent silence, the words becoming part of the worshipper's body and mind.

On Krynn, the followers of {@deity Paladine|Dragonlance|DSotDQ} (patron deity to the gods of Good) uphold sacred feasting rites during high holy days, including the Feast of Gratitude, featuring {@recipe Roast Gammon Pie|HFLotT}, a comfort dish so divine that it transcends location, unbound by plane or realm. In stark contrast, cults of {@deity Chemosh|Dragonlance|DSotDQ} or {@deity Morgion|Dragonlance|DSotDQ} may host symbolic meals of blackened roots and blood-colored wines, meant to remind followers of death's ever-present reach. These meals are sparse and ritualized, serving more as devotional ordeal than nourishment.

In Eberron, where faith intersects with invention, divine meals are often portable and efficient, yet still sacred. The followers of {@deity the Silver Flame|Eberron|ERLW} produce Emberbread, a dense, flame-kissed biscuit meant to sustain for days. Said to "burn evil from within," Emberbread is a common ration for itinerant clerics. In Sharn's sky-temples, the faithful of {@deity Boldrei|Eberron|ERLW} serve Sanctified Pottage ladled from brass cauldrons, available to anyone in need regardless of creed. Blessings are expressed between each serving, brief prayers woven into the act of giving. Boldrei's Feast, a holiday on the ninth of Rhaan, is a communal feast celebrated across Khorvaire overseen by her many devout clerics.

Amid the endless convergence of pantheons in Sigil, the City of Doors, the food of the faithful is astonishingly diverse. Wandering clerics of {@deity Lathander|Faerûnian|FRHoF} offer {@recipe Barovian Garlic Bread|HFLotT} imbued with restorative magic said to reinvigorate the sick and ward off the undead. In Sigil, one can dine on gnomish fermented fungus stew, sacred elven fasting breads, or a celestial {@recipe Holiday Rib Roast|HFLotT} (this page) prepared in the upper halls of Mount Celestia, all within a few blocks, if you know the right door to knock on.

entries.name: The Spirit in the Meal
entries: For clerics, food is never just food. It is a sacrament, a symbol, a tool of healing and faith. Where wizards dazzle, clerics comfort. Where druids enchant, clerics bless. They believe the divine can be tasted in a warm slice of bread, whispered in the fragrance of steeping herbs, and shared with anyone who finds themselves hungry in body or soul. Across the multiverse, no matter the deity or domain, the table is a holy place. And when a cleric serves a meal, it is an invitation to experience the divine one bite at a time.

data.name: Druid

entries: If you must protest, I respond only to hunger strikes and, even then, too late.
entries.by: Jaheira, Druid of The Circle of the Land

entries: Passionate protectors of nature, {@class Druid|XPHB|druids} are the allies and nurturers of all that is natural in the multiverse. Sometimes called "Nature Priests of Primal Power," they live among forests, jungles, and other locales unspoiled by industry and civilization. Rather than trying to master the wilds, druids consider themselves an extension of it, using their wiles, survivalist grit, and substantial natural magic to serve as nature's stewards and sometimes even its wrath. Whether followers of nature-oriented gods or nature itself—called the "Old Faith"—druids believe that there is a natural form, function, and process in everything, and food is a necessary part of that cycle. Consequently, druids choose and prepare foods that are natural, wholesome, sustainable, and minimally disruptive to whatever local ecosystem they find themselves in.

entries.name: One with Nature
entries: When a druid dwells among nature, they are never without. Every leaf, branch, insect, and animal plays a part in the natural order, and the druid both protects that balance and sustains themselves within it. Not only are they exceptional foragers due to their knowledge of edible plants, herbs, and spices, but their connection to the wild makes them wily trappers and hunters when the need demands. This is especially apparent when in {@classFeature Wild Shape|Druid|XPHB|2|XPHB}, where they assume the form, talents, and sometimes tastes of their beast allies. For example, a druid who seeks larger game for a hungry party stranded in the wilderness might assume the form of a panther to track a fleet-of-foot elk.

Druids can also use their nature-powered magic to lend a hand in sourcing and preparation. While few druids eat meat, those who do can use simple incantations such as {@spell snare|XGE} to catch their prey and then {@spell create bonfire|XGE} to quickly cook up the meal. They can also use their powers to commune with and find animals and plants to aid in sourcing. In desperate cases, some druids have been known to conjure a swarm of insects not to overwhelm enemies but to provide a simple, high-protein meal for a party of starved adventurers. In all cases, humane and sustainable sourcing is paramount for the druid.

entries.name: Nature's Cupboard
entries: The tastes and ingredients of the druid are highly dependent on both their locale and their personal beliefs. Virtually all druids would be inclined to use a combination of sustainable and locally sourced plants, herbs, and spices in their everyday cooking, but many gravitate to ingredients and flavors from flora they consider sacred, such as juniper, oak, and birch. In hotter, dryer climes, cactus plants and yucca trees hold a similar reverence, while various mushrooms are celebrated in many areas of the Underdark and Feywild.

However, the most significant factor that guides the druid's diet, ingredients, and foodways is their loosely knit society known as a "circle," which supports and influences their specific beliefs. For example, a member of the {@subclass Land|Druid|XPHB|XPHB|Circle of the Land} is driven by protecting ancient traditions and knowledge, which includes sacred rites, festivals, and the recipes that go along with them. Meanwhile, those of the {@subclass Moon|Druid|XPHB|XPHB|Circle of the Moon} are fierce protectors of the deepest wilds and are less inclined to eat meat or make any impacts on the natural ecosystem. The druids of the {@subclass Sea|Druid|XPHB|XPHB|Circle of the Sea} revel in the powers of the wind and water and are inclined to sustainably forage their meals from oceans, lakes, and rivers, while those of the {@subclass Stars|Druid|XPHB|XPHB|Circle of the Stars} have tastes as diverse as the very cosmos they gaze upon.

entries.name: The Nature of the Multiverse
entries: Nature comes in many forms across the multiverse. As druids can be found on every realm, it follows that they are as diverse as the very natural habitats they call home, as are their customs, beliefs, and foodways.

Druids of the planet Oerth are most inclined to worship nature itself as adherents of the Old Faith. However, it is not uncommon for these forest dwellers to also venerate nature-oriented gods such as {@deity Beory|Greyhawk|XDMG}, the Oerth Mother, as well as {@deity Ehlonna|Greyhawk|XDMG}, {@deity Obad-Hai|Greyhawk|XDMG}, and {@deity Ulaa|Greyhawk|XDMG}. From the Burneal Forest of northern reaches of the Flanaess near Blackmoor to the Dreadwood of Keoland in the south, druids of this world roam their sacred wilds gathering fruits, vegetables, herbs, and spices to make their own variations of {@recipe Everything Soup|HF}. Those who are in search of effective healing remedies might be on the lookout for plump berries, which they can transmute into {@spell goodberry|XPHB|goodberries} for use in a tasty {@recipe Goodberry Blend|HF} elixir.

The continent of Faerûn of the planet Toril is teeming with druids in its myriad forests, jungles, and grasslands unspoiled by the engines of industry. They venerate the nature gods of the "First Circle," who include {@deity Silvanus|Faerûnian|FRHoF}; {@deity Mielikki|Faerûnian|FRHoF}; {@deity Chauntea|Faerûnian|FRHoF}; and even gods of nature's destructive power such as {@deity Talos|Faerûnian|FRHoF}, {@deity Auril|Faerûnian|FRHoF}, and {@deity Umberlee|Faerûnian|FRHoF}. Druids of the High Forest live in harmony with local elves, often sharing in a fresh bowl of {@recipe Wild Strawberry Salad|HFLotT}. The druids of Neverwinter Wood often commune with nature-loving Fey creatures who frequently emerge from the local Fey Crossing bringing with them their legendary {@recipe Feywild Eggs|HF}, making the dish a favorite of druids on both sides of reality.

The druids of Eberron are less inclined to recognize that world's commonly held pantheon of the Sovereign Host or the Dark Six and instead believe that every element of nature, from the sun and stars to the soil and fire, has its own spirit. This belief carries over to ingredients and food as well. While each sect, from the Gatekeepers and Children of Winter to the Ashbound, has their own philosophy on their roles as protectors, they all agree that their natural magic is a way to command and communicate with these spirits and that certain recipes, such as {@recipe Root Vegetables, Gratin-Style|HFLotT}, are not only delicious but help the spirits coalesce.

The druids of Abanasinia of the world Krynn often share the forests with the nature-loving Qualinesti elves of the west and Silvanesti elves of the east and recipes along with them. {@recipe Qualinesti Vegetable Stew|HF} has since become a favorite of druids not just across the planet but the multiverse.

entries.name: The Circle of Food
entries: No matter where you find them, from the lushest forests of Ansalon to the deepest jungles of Chult, druids are protectors of the world around them, even while exposing and cultivating some of its most extraordinary natural flavors. They use their substantial practical and magical talents of nature to source foods and ingredients that are fresh, clean, sustainable, and delicious. While their cuisine is as diverse as the worlds they traverse, it can be all but assured that a party with a druid on board will never go hungry in the wilderness.

data.name: Fighter

entries: Yer pardon, fair lady. Might I be getting a bit o' food?
entries.by: Bruenor Battlehammer, Fighter and King of Mithral Hall and Gauntlgrym

entries: {@class Fighter|XPHB|Fighters} are masters of the battlefield. Experts of arms and armament, these fearless warriors typically inhabit the front lines of combat, charging bravely into battle using a combination of martial skill, tactics, and brawn to win the day while gathering the well-earned spoils of war in the process. Among the most diverse of adventuring types, fighters come from all backgrounds and walks of life, from knights and soldiers to gladiators and mercenaries. However, one thing they all have in common is a need to eat, and fighters across the multiverse have proven that they have not only a taste for combat but also for delicious food. For the fighter, the rules of dining are simple: Satiate the appetite, nourish the body, and save the celebration for after the day is won.

entries.name: Martial Masters
entries: The term "fighter" encompasses warriors of all shapes, sizes, and battle styles, from masters of blades, bows, and hammers to clubs, maces, and polearms. Some even use a deadly combination of martial prowess mixed with arcane magic or psionic powers of the mind. It follows then that the foods they prepare and prefer are as distinctive as their fighting styles and implements of war. For example, a {@subclass Battle Master|Fighter|XPHB|XPHB} who specializes in complex combat techniques and tactics prefers cooking methods that are equally so. From butchering to braising, precision and skill are the hallmarks of their cuisine. The {@subclass Champion|Fighter|XPHB|XPHB}, on the other hand, is a creature of pure bravery and brawn, and their dishes invariably have bold elements of flavor, usually along with a few risks that are sure to guarantee glorious culinary victory or the flavors of ignominious defeat.

The {@subclass Eldritch Knight|Fighter|XPHB|XPHB} blends their skills on the battlefield with an array of arcane magic and is inclined toward concoctions every bit as complex and potent as the battlefield incantations they cast. While little is known about the tastes of {@subclass Psi Warrior|Fighter|XPHB|XPHB|Psi Warriors} due to their rarity, it is said that these fighters often cook their victory meals without lifting a finger, yet still the knives chop, spoons stir, and spices shake all through their powers of the mind. Perhaps the most distinctive of all is the {@subclass Dungeoneer|Fighter|XPHB|ValdaPlayerPack} who, by preference or necessity, has come into the habit of preparing freshly slain monsters for their meals—fangs, claws, poisons, and all.

entries.name: Well-Rounded Flavors
entries: The fighter is a survivor in all respects, and this instinct applies not only to the battlefield but also to the wilds. Their exceptional combat skills often carry over to tracking and hunting wild animals and monsters. While not as crafty or precise in the wilderness as the {@class ranger|XPHB}, the fighter is gritty and resourceful and will more often than not get the job done. Whether on the trail or at the tavern, fighters typically prefer meat-based meals, gravitating toward common proteins such as rabbit, deer, pheasant, boar, turkey, ham, {@creature rothé|VGM}, and {@creature stirge|XPHB}. However, lighter fare, such as fruits, vegetables, and {@recipe Chopforest|HFFotM}, is also on the table, especially before battle to ensure top performance. Many fighters who have served in the military are well practiced at dealing with meager portions and continual hunger during a siege or march, so they can find themselves contented with simple {@recipe Iron Rations|HF} for extended periods of time.

When it comes to preparation, fighters tend to be practical and watchful, avoiding recipes that are so involved that they leave the party open to ambush. This often means simple, meat-based stews and other single-pan or skillet-cooked meals. When afforded the time, many fighters make excellent butchers due to their exceptional skill with the blade. Consequently, many fighters are known as masters of the grill and spit, creating delicious steaks and roasts from their latest kill.

entries.name: Realms of Battle
entries: No matter where one roams in the multiverse, where there are people, there is conflict. Thus, fighters are numerous on all realms, as natural to each world as its soil and the crops that grow upon it.

Fighters of the oft war-torn Krynn are sure to find comfort and nourishment in the world's many outstanding roadside taverns, such as the Inn of the Last Home, where {@recipe Otik's Skillet-Fried Spiced Potatoes|HF|Otik's Potatoes} are so beloved that fighters have been known to re-create this recipe across the multiverse. {@recipe Bangers and Smash|HF} is another tavern favorite, imported directly from the dwarves of Thorbardin of the Khalkist Mountains. Fighters traversing the lands of Solamnia will no doubt find themselves most at home upon the battlements of one of its many great cities or castles, slurping up fresh {@recipe Solstice Soup|HFLotT} and sipping upon the {@recipe Dwarven Mulled Wine|HF|Mulled Wine} popularized by Lord Gunthar, Grand Master of the Knights of Solamnia.

The world of Eberron is also no stranger to war, the lands still teeming with fighters both retired and active. Those who dwell in the northeastern military nation of Karrnath often prepare a hearty mushroom dinner bread called {@recipe Vedbread|HF} that can be consumed while on the march. When afforded a short rest, those same fighters delight in a skillet-style meal of eggs, sausage, and red peppers they call the {@recipe Blood of Vol|HFFotM}, named after a popular religious philosophy of self-reliance and the "divinity within." The warriors of Eberron's central Khorvaire nation of Thrane are similarly inclined toward simple, fast, single-pan cooking in their dishes such as {@recipe Thrakel-Seared Beef in Red Sauce|HFFotM}, a flavorful stir-fry of flank steak and fresh vegetables.

Fighters of Toril are as numerous as the stars of Realmspace, delving the world's countless dungeons and lairs in search of untold treasures. Those who delve the notorious Undermountain of Waterdeep are sure to imbibe a tankard or two of {@recipe Undermountain Alurlyath|HFFotM} to gain the "silver glow"—which some insist is the false confidence that comes with drink—before descending to the dungeon's first level from the well in the Yawning Portal tavern. In the unlikely event they return, the newly treasure-laden fighters might celebrate with {@recipe Sembian Honey-Glazed Rothé Ribs|HF|Honey-Glazed Rothé Ribs} or some {@recipe Spicy Shredded Stirge Sliders|HFDoMM}. However, great meals are as abundant in the wilds as they are in the world's great metropolises. Accordingly, fighters of this realm need not be orcs to enjoy {@recipe "Orc" Bacon|HF|Orc Bacon} or even the {@recipe Braised Lamb|HF} of orcs of the Cold Lands—both common dishes prepared by fighters on the trail to adventure.

Steeped in long traditions of chivalry and heraldry, the fighters and knights of Oerth are much inclined toward celebratory feasts after victorious battles. {@recipe Sornstag|HFFotM|Venison Sornstag} and {@recipe Hommlet Golden Brown Roasted Turkey with Sausage Stuffing and Drippings|HF|Hommlet Golden Brown Roasted Turkey} are favorites of these castle hearths. However, less fanciful meals are far more the norm, such as the fried egg, sausage, and potato skillet called {@recipe Quij's Plate|HFFotM}, sometimes cooked up in haste on a kite shield. Those who wander too far off the trail and into the mists might eventually find themselves guests at Castle Ravenloft feasting upon {@recipe Whole Roast Boar|HFFotM} even as the gracious host, {@creature Strahd von Zarovich|RHW|Strahd}, prepares for a meal of his own among the diners.

entries.name: Kitchen Warriors
entries: Whether on the front lines of battle or the kitchen, there are few better allies to have on your side than the fighter. Gritty and practical, they gravitate toward quick, meat-based meals that keep them nourished and satisfied but can make do with whatever the circumstances allow. From light pre-battle snacks to grand post-battle feasts, the food of the fighter is bound to be simple, nutritious, and delicious.

data.name: Monk

entries: Before you attempt to ride the remorhaz, I might suggest you take a hearty meal. Otherwise, it may be the remorhaz who makes a meal of you. Either way, the cycle of life continues.

To a {@class monk|XPHB}, the spirit is a mirror of the body, and through one's physicality the mind and soul are channeled. As such, the body of a monk is quite literally a temple, an edifice where the mortal comes in contact with the divine. The discipline that monks exercise over their body and the control that comes with it are legendary. The cycle of life and the flow of focus from one living body to another make the diet of a monk a serious matter. They dine with purpose, whether alone or with their order, honoring their bodies and their food in ceremonial harmony.

entries.name: From Monastery to Meadhall
entries: Most monks begin their careers in a monastery, in a communal setting where producing meals is a group effort. Cooking is never drudgery to a monk—it is its own ritual, meticulously timed and requiring the judicious combination of carefully selected components. Monks bring this temperament to their dining in the broader world.

Not all monks eschew blades, but many prefer to work ingredients with their bare hands, having no need for cuts. If a monk must kill to prepare a meal, it is always a considered death. They tend to be unimpressed by trinkets and baubles and have no interest in silver spoons or fancy plates. Many are happy to dine with the simplest implements on the crudest platters.

Sharing a meal with fellow contemplatives in a monastic setting may not be as boisterous as an adventurer's tavern, but it bestows a common appreciation of our dependence on the material world. Monks convey that same appreciation to any meal they share with others. Even those monks who have entirely transcended the need for food and water partake in meals with their friends to feel the kinship of dining together.

entries.name: Meals and Meditations
entries: Monks eat not just to sustain their bodies, but to hone their focus. It has been said that monks have an uncanny metabolism. They choose what to eat in consideration of how they will apply the energy gained; a monk would not wallow in gluttony, partaking no more than is needed. As dramatically as monks can change their own bodies, their powers do not require them to ingest any sort of specific fuel to unlock abilities. It is not the case that monks who favor fiery breath weapons, say, must ingest a bit more pepper and spices, or ginger and garlic—in fact, they might prefer more soothing repasts.

{@subclass Open Hand|Monk|XPHB|XPHB|Warriors of the Open Hand} tend to seek out more protein-forward dishes, even meats and cheeses, to power their incessant flurries of rapid strikes. The more subtle {@subclass Shadow|Monk|XPHB|XPHB|Warriors of Shadow} may favor leaner, more neutral fare like soups and calming teas that steady the hand for delicate, quiet operations. {@subclass Elements|Monk|XPHB|XPHB|Warriors of the Elements} may seek out temperatures and flavors compatible with the elemental affinities they frequently choose. The mask-clad {@subclass Mercy|Monk|XPHB|XPHB|Warriors of Mercy} often take their food raw, experiencing its most essential nature.

Powerful monks have been known to willingly ingest the deadliest of poisons, which pose no threat to such an advanced practitioner, but nonetheless offer otherworldly flavors and a strong reminder of the ephemerality of existence. This is a lesson as valuable to those who take lives as to those who save them.

entries.name: The Manifold Path
entries: Even a monk dedicated to an order knows that everyone walks their own path. It is said some monks who live under the strictest vows of poverty eat only what they are given as charity, and thus must eat quite indiscriminately. At the opposite extreme, there are rumored to be monks whose fighting style is based on copious amounts of alcohol consumption.

An itinerant monk may prefer simple fare eaten on the go, even finger food like {@recipe Goldenstars|HFFotM} or {@recipe Cloaks|HFFotM} while in town or foraged salads in the wild. But the most characteristic meals of monks are those made at their temples and monasteries throughout the multiverse.

In the Bloodstone Lands of Faerûn, the initiates serving at the mountainside Monastery of the Yellow Rose lead a hardscrabble life. Working sometimes sixteen hours a day, they tirelessly haul ice from the Great Glacier to be melted down into water and either forage the cliffs or tend to what gardens they can muster. They can, however, produce enough blueberry to make a serviceable {@recipe Potion of Restoration|HF}. And as devotees of {@deity Ilmater|Faerûnian|FRHoF} and St. Sollars the Twice-Martyred, they are well respected and sure to be well fed wherever hospitality is to be found.

In Greyhawk, the sinister Scarlet Order schemes to overthrow the Flanaess in the name of an ancient bloodline. The monks can thus be found infiltrating any institution of importance, where they indulge their appetites as the demands of the subterfuge require. Their hidden monastery, which resides on the southerly Tilvanot Peninsula, is where they hatch their schemes. Observers suspect that the Brotherhood developed their taste for {@recipe Yuan-Ti Ceremonial Soup|HFLotT} from some collusion with Hepmonaland. But it is said monks in Faerûn also favor that refreshing vegetable soup, so there may well be other paths of transmission.

The kalashtar followers of the Path of Shadows who travel in Khorvaire have left behind their monasteries in remote Adar. As fusions of humans with the outsiders known as the quori, the kalashtar mostly reside in their temple keeps, but their desire to do good in the broader world of Eberron leads the most fearless of them to the distant reaches of the world. Some of those who returned brought with them a taste for {@recipe Blackroot Tal with Honey|HFLotT} and the know-how to make it.

entries.name: Culinary Mastery
entries: The life of a monk is one of discipline and structure, of routines and rituals. The primal rhythms of life, breathing, and eating connect the monk with everyone and everything around them. For some, the structures of a monastery guide these activities in productive directions, but others must find their way in the world with nothing but a handful of friends to rely on. The companionship of a monk can make even the most thoughtless eater appreciate the wonders of food.

data.name: Paladin

entries: You may have forsworn your oath, but your oath hasn't forsworn you.

{@class Paladin|XPHB|Paladins} derive their power from an oath: from uttering a conviction so deep and so certain that it becomes the source of world-altering magic. It may be an oath to defend the helpless, to preserve what matters most, or to avenge something or someone lost. Whatever its subject, the oath takes precedence over all else in a paladin's life, with force that can both smite the wicked and heal the sick. It governs the paladin's interactions with others, their relationship with property, and even their attitudes toward food. No paladin sworn to uphold justice could eat while another goes hungry, and any sustenance taken by a paladin serves as fuel for their oath.

entries.name: Divine Demeanor
entries: Because a paladin's oath takes precedence over their very lives, paladins cannot be self-centered or particularly self-interested. A paladin's grumbling belly is unlikely to be their highest priority: They view dining as a way to nurture others first and themselves secondarily. Paladins never want to take the first bowl or the first slice—indeed, many paladins fast for a day or more at a time in their ascetic devotions. But when they do eat, they make it count.

Although the magic of a paladin is not essentially divine in origin—it comes from within, even when it is divinely inspired—it has much in common with clerical magic. Even novice paladins can learn to {@spell Purify Food and Drink|XPHB|purify drink and water} and to {@spell Detect Poison and Disease|XPHB|detect poisons}; when sharing a plate with a paladin, you can chow down with confidence. More experienced paladins can even {@spell create food and water|XPHB} directly.

Food created by magic can save the day in an emergency, but any paladin would prefer to be more hands-on. When their other responsibilities permit, paladins make for attentive cooks. It has been remarked that paladins are no strangers to blades, and they are more than equal to the task of hunting wild game on their mounts if such is required.

entries.name: Devotion and Glory
entries: Some paladin oaths, or the strictures of their orders, may come with dietary constraints. But otherwise, paladins favor simple, healthy food above lavish dishes. Any paladin will eat heartily to maintain their physical powers, as feats of arms do not come easily on an empty stomach. But for the most part, paladins with access to a larder would serve themselves simple bread, soups, and vegetable-forward dishes, as meats might be considered an extravagance. That said, there are times when ceremony and celebration call for something grander, and paladins understand how inspiring such occasions can be for the people who need inspiration most.

{@subclass Devotion|Paladin|XPHB|XPHB|Oath of Devotion} paladins set an example of righteousness that all can follow, and that would extend to their choice of meals. A paladin who has taken the {@subclass Ancients|Paladin|XPHB|XPHB|Oath of the Ancients} would delight in the finest culinary efforts and might be found seeking acclaimed chefs and the most artistic food preparations, but having time-honored and traditional ingredients would be of equal importance. An {@subclass Glory|Paladin|XPHB|XPHB|Oath of Glory} paladin might stage a lavish banquet to commemorate a spectacular victory, though it would be a feast mostly intended for others to consume, to help cement the memory of an occasion for the ages.

Although they have a reputation for being stern or even severe, paladins can make very personable company. A meal created and served by a paladin creates its own sort of aura, enlivening the paladin's companions and bestowing them with strength and resilience.

entries.name: Knights in Shining Armor
entries: Many paladins willfully live in poverty and crusade alone as itinerant knights, taking the burden of their oaths entirely upon themselves. But eliminating wickedness from an entire world is not a solo quest. Paladins often find themselves a member of an order that shares and to some degree determines their ideals and goals.

Counted among the Knights of Solamnia in Krynn, there are many paladins and some few branches of knighthood to which they might aspire. The oath that every such knight swears is simple and profound: "My honor is my life." These orders are known for their righteousness, the formality of their etiquette, and their strict codes of conduct. {@feat Knight of the Sword|DSotDQ|Knights in the Order of Sword} must eat nothing for one day each week; {@feat Knight of the Rose|DSotDQ|Rose Knights} must abstain from alcoholic beverages and other perceived vices like gambling. Everything such a knight needs can be found in a simple cup of {@recipe Solamnic Mushroom Ragout with Dumplings|HFLotT}.

The paladins of the {@background Knight of the Gauntlet|FRHoF|Order of the Gauntlet} operate throughout Faerûn, acting wherever necessary to counter the influence of the sinister Cult of the Dragon. Any tavern could be their local base of operations, like the Pair of Black Antlers in Elturel, where they might be found dining on {@recipe Gurdats|HF}. It is said the new recruits of the order, who are known as Gallants, keep to the simplest fare, such as {@recipe Corn and Lentil Soup|HFLotT}—their wills bent entirely on defending the weak and smiting evil.

The Purified, as the paladins of {@deity the Silver Flame|Eberron|ERLW} in Khorvaire call themselves, are bound to the Tenet of Purity—a call to "burn the corruption and taint of evil from all Eberron." Many paladins of the Order of Templars skip a meal on the first day of the week, the Day of Cleansing Fire, and the most devout will fast the entire day. But one of the Silver Flame's thirteen high holy days is Baker's Night, when treats and pastries are shared among friends and families of the faithful. A special favorite of that celebration is the {@recipe Skyway Special|HFLotT}, a dish usually reserved for the privileged but available for all when it is time for a feast.

But between those paladins who walk their path alone and those who belong to a grand order, there are many who keep the simple society of a group of trusted friends with whom they adventure, strive, and of course eat. The company of a paladin is not everyone's cup of tea, but those who have the privilege of calling a paladin a friend know that there is no more heartening person to share a kettle with.

entries.name: The Path
entries: The path of righteous is not promised to be a leisurely one; luxury is not often part of a paladin's life. Paladins can spare no time for indulgence and repose while the wicked thrive and the weak suffer. Through their oaths, paladins hope to make the world a better place, a place where comfort is not a stranger to anyone. On the day of victory, they will lead the toast at the celebratory feast.

data.name: Ranger

entries: The cat wants you to come along. It'll be better than a cave, and better food than half-cooked fish.

{@class Ranger|XPHB|Rangers} are the wilderness warriors, scouts, and survivalists of the multiverse. They are also guardians and wardens of the wild, standing vigil on the front lines of settlements to protect from wandering natural threats. Often solitary by nature or profession, they are deeply tied to the land, attuned to its rhythms and resources. And when it comes to food, rangers are more than just self-sufficient; they're artists of the wild pantry. From hunting and foraging to fire-roasted feasts under star-filled skies, rangers help keep companions on course and well fed while on an adventure.

entries.name: Forms of the Hunter
entries: A ranger's talents and magic are honed with deadly focus to protect the world from monsters and tyrants. As such, ranger's tastes and expertise are personified by the very skills they study. A {@subclass Beast Master|Ranger|XPHB|XPHB} ranger who shares a mystical bond with their animal companion may expertly track their prey. A {@subclass Hunter|Ranger|XPHB|XPHB} hones their predatory instincts into an art form, knowing just when to strike for a clean, ethical kill. A {@subclass Gloom Stalker|Ranger|XPHB|XPHB} not only pursues foes that lurk in darkness, but they are also extremely proficient at procuring uncommon sustenance. And a mirthful {@subclass Fey Wanderer|Ranger|XPHB|XPHB} sees the whole world as their larder.

In most parties, rangers serve the role of forager, cook, and quartermaster, responsible for tracking and hunting. In the multiverse, rangers adapt to the cultural culinary traditions of their realms. These regional traditions may even become part of the ranger's identity and are often a bridge to different cultures they encounter.

entries.name: The Green Pantry
entries: From the primal jungles of Chult to the dreamy twilight of the Feywild, ranger cuisine is deeply regional and resourceful. Each world brings unique flora, fauna, climates, and cultures, and rangers adapt their survival and cooking techniques accordingly.

Some rangers follow nonlethal methods when hunting, preferring to trap or capture small game in honor of the balance of nature. Others are unparalleled hunters with an arsenal of options at their disposal, including longbows or crossbows. These survivalists understand the migratory patterns of birds and fish and are adept at identifying ideal game, fat-rich in winter, lean and tender in spring.

As natural explorers, rangers can also forage efficiently in varied terrains, often gathering berries, mushrooms, roots, and herbs. A ranger's knowledge includes not just what is edible but what pairs well.

entries.name: A Taste of the Trail
entries: Rangers are practical cooks, but that doesn't mean their meals are bland. A good ranger can craft a savory stew with nothing more than an old pot, a bed of hot stones, and the right selection of herbs. At their disposal is a myriad of campfire techniques including "Split-Log Fire" in which a halved log with kindling inside burns hot and long for grilling meat; the "Stone Ring Method" in which heat-retaining rocks are arranged in a circle for slow cooking; and the "Clay Bake," an old elven trick that involves encasing meat or fish in mud then cooking it under coals to seal in the flavor.

For a ranger, cooking is a ritual to ground themselves, honor the creatures they've hunted, and bond with allies. Some ranger dishes might include the pragmatic yet flavorful golden-crusted {@recipe River Fish Fry|HFLotT} or Basilisk Broth, which is said to grant temporary resistance to poison (with the right alchemical preparation). When in need of something on the go, a simple Mushroom Jerky, dried over embers and smoked with hickory bark, may well do the trick.

Though not as overtly magical as druids or wizards, rangers do possess spells that enhance their relationship to food and nature. One of their most important survival food spells, {@spell goodberry|XPHB}, is a staple for healing and nourishment. {@spell Speak with animals|XPHB} enables ethical hunting through consent or gaining knowledge about local game from wildlife. Useful not just for taming companions, {@spell animal friendship|XPHB} is a great spell for negotiating with intelligent beasts instead of hunting them. And when time is of the essence, {@spell locate animals or plants|XPHB} helps them pinpoint elusive herbs, rare fruits, or specific game creatures.

entries.name: Wild Wanderers
entries: In every corner of the vast multiverse, where civilization thins and wild terrain dominates, rangers learn to live off the land with whatever nature provides.

The continent of Faerûn is a microcosm of the planet Toril's extremely varied climates and cultures. In the Dalelands, rangers forage mushrooms, wild onions, and herbs, cooking easily sourced game in hot stones and ash pits. Elven rangers tend toward lighter, herbaceous fare such as Berry-Glazed Venison. Goliath rangers in the frigid Spine of the World focus on survival staples like Lichen Stew thickened with powdered bone. The Mulhorandi desert rangers of Faerûn roast Spiced Locusts and preserve meat in sun-dried citrus rinds. Rangers in the Chultan jungles survive on massive fruits like jackfruit or durian, fire-roasted grubs, and Spit-Roasted Dinosaur, basted with coconut oil and jungle peppers.

Eberron's fusion of magic and steam-tech influences ranger cuisine. Here, ranger meals can be enhanced by cooking tools or dragonmarked spices. Q'barran jungle rangers might prepare a pot of Crocodile "Thighs and Eyes" Bouillabaisse over a portable arcane stove. Thranes favor food blessed with minor enchantments to resist spoilage or poison. Even {@race Warforged|EFA} rangers, who usually require no food, often craft meals out of tradition for morale and meaning.

In the Feywild, a plane of inspired beauty where senses are heightened, rangers have developed a dreamlike culinary style. Food here feels alive, sparkling, and often has strange magical effects. In this ethereal realm, meals glimmer with bioluminescence, flowers might bloom into decadent pastries, and butterflies could taste like the sweetest honeyed figs. It's often said that a traveler hasn't truly tasted the Feywild unless they've sampled an ooey-gooey slice of {@recipe Duskmallow Pie|HFLotT}.

The Shadowfell, the antithetical plane of existence to the Feywild, is a bleak expanse of black terrain, twisted forests, and sparse resources. Here, ranger meals are utilitarian but clever, with ingredients including bitter root and creatures like shadow hares or gloom owls. They seek foods that are high in calories, such as smoked meat soaked in shadow vinegar and broth boiled with bone and dark herbs.

In the void between stars, in the region known as Wildspace, rangers aboard spelljamming vessels must get creative. Foraging might entail milking a floating sky-ray, harvesting edible crystal fungi, or scraping nutrient-rich moss off asteroid rock. An astral ranger could serve up {@recipe Spiced Pork and Orange Peppers|HFFotM} for a sojourn across the stars. Here, most meals are lightweight, nutrient-packed, often reconstituted with heat or magic.

entries.name: Wild Soul, Warm Meal
entries: Ranger cuisine is more than survival; it's ritual, resilience, and the quiet comfort of something warm when the world feels cold and overwhelming. To be a ranger is to live with the land not merely on it; to move through the wilds with purpose, respect, and an unshakable bond to nature. This connection extends to the way they eat—practical yet reverent, nourishing both body and spirit. Whether they're snaring pheasants, roasting mushrooms over coals, or conjuring a life-sustaining berry, rangers ensure no one goes hungry...even at the edge of the world.
