data.name: Rogue

entries: What 'tis?! A roadside food stall serving yet more scrumptious morsels in this most delicious of realms?! This I must investigate!

Masters of stealth, agility, and deception, {@class Rogue|XPHB|rogues} populate the shadows of the multiverse in search of luxury and loot. While many live on the wrong side of the law, an adventuring party would be foolish to not have one of these scrappy scoundrels around to pick locks, scale walls, find traps, or even orchestrate a con. Their professions tend to be as varied as their skill sets, ranging from simple thieves and pickpockets to cutthroats, assassins, and even tricksters who use petty arcane spells or psionic powers to meet their ends. No matter their specialty, it's usually feast or famine for these resourceful survivors, which applies as much to their day-to-day lives as to the food they consume. The rogue is always in search of their next score or meal and will take everything they can get when they can get it, seeking as much richness in their food as in their purses.

entries.name: Masters of Shadow
entries: The talents of the rogue are many, ranging from {@skill sleight of hand|XPHB}, moving silently and picking locks to climbing walls, disappearing into shadows, or unleashing lethal strikes unseen. They are masters of evasion, whether it be the blows of enemies or the law, and some even dabble in illusionary arcane magic or psionic mind powers to enhance their skills of trickery and offense. With such broad skill sets, it is no wonder that their cooking and dining preferences are equally so. For example, those who work primarily as {@subclass Thief|Rogue|XPHB|XPHB|Thieves} have grown accustomed to taking what they get and most often find themselves cooking and eating on the run. Ever watchful, they tend to avoid the traps of overcooking, while their dexterity allows them to easily pick up sometimes complicated techniques. Meanwhile, few can butcher steaks, cut vegetables, or slice fruit with the precision of the {@subclass Assassin|Rogue|XPHB|XPHB}. Between their extraordinary skill with the blade and their penchant for surprises, the meals of these killers are sure to include hidden and unexpected flavors that delight.

The cuisine of {@subclass Arcane Trickster|Rogue|XPHB|XPHB|Arcane Tricksters} is nearly as hard to pin down as the scoundrels themselves. Based on their skill and familiarity with arcane magic, they have little trouble following or concocting complicated recipes and usually add some illusory flair as special touch. Like other spellcasters, they typically find help in the kitchen with incantations such as mage hand or will use minor illusions in their presentations to dazzle their diners. The mysterious {@subclass Soulknife|Rogue|XPHB|XPHB}, on the other hand, has the habit of using the remarkable psychic blades they can manifest in their preparations even while whispering appetizing suggestions directly into the minds of their diners. The {@subclass Mastermind|Rogue|XPHB|XGE} needs no such subtle suggestions in their dining and is far more inclined to eat the meal than prepare it.

entries.name: Shade-Grown Ingredients
entries: Regardless of their profession, the rogue most often lives on the fringes of society. Simple, light, and easy-to-eat produce, such as apples, carrots, plums, peaches, and strawberries, usually pilfered from market carts, is a favorite of these shady professionals who live and work on the run. {@recipe Iron rations|HF}, dried meats, seeds, and nuts play a similar role upon the trail, where practicality trumps enjoyment. However, when time and safety allow, the rogue is known to love preparing and indulging in some of the most decadent meals and desserts of any group. In fact, it is said the secretive banquets held among thieves' guilds are legendary in their flavors and extravagance.

From a preparation standpoint, rogues are often capable of cooking elaborate dishes but always while keeping both their potatoes and eyes peeled. While modest soups and single-pan meals are common dishes on the trail, when given access to a proper kitchen, rogues have a way of surprising the party with a sneak attack of flavor consisting of delicious pastries, cakes, and sweets. In these situations, their tastes go from practical to palatial, favoring sweet and savory flavors ranging from cheese and smoked meats to maple syrup, walnuts, berries, and sweet cream. In this respect, rogues seem to have drawn much influence from halflings, possibly due to all the famous thieves and burglars who have emerged from the species.

entries.name: Food and Flight
entries: Where there is need, there are rogues also. So, it should come as no surprise that these scallywags inhabit every realm of the multiverse. While their inclination is to keep a low profile, their presence is often made known by powerful thieves' guilds that dominate not only the community and culture of rogues but their tastes in food also.

On the world of Toril, the notorious Shadow Thieves of Amn are renowned for their luxurious tastes, having pilfered numerous legendary recipes, from the {@recipe Honeyed Ham with Pineapple Gravy|HF|Honey Ham with Pineapple Gravy} of Luiren to the {@recipe Sour Cream-Walnut Cake|HFFotM|Sour Cream Walnut Cake} of the Yawning Portal. Meanwhile, the infamous thieves' guild of Pasha Basadoni in Calimport prefer {@recipe Fig Cakes|HFFotM} while on the move and {@recipe Double-High Halfling Pie|HFLotT} when celebrating their latest heist. On the planet Oerth, the Guild of Thieves of Greyhawk seem to share similar tastes, often wolfing down decadent {@recipe Halfling Oatmeal Sweet Nibbles|HF} while on the lam or on the prowl.

While thieves' guilds are not recognized upon the planet Eberron, their activities are alive and well in the major cities, courtesy of various criminal enterprises and even some of the shadier houses. For example, House Tarkanan supplies their fair share of underhanded assassins and rogues, who often celebrate their successes with the {@recipe Fruit and Ricotta Pancakes|HFLotT} and {@recipe Silverfruit Pie|HFFotM} on offer at the Celestial Vista in Sharn. Far across the multiverse, on the planet Krynn, powerful thieves' guilds are few, yet rogues are many, often gravitating to the decadent treats of the Kender, such as {@recipe Kender loaf|HFFotM} and {@recipe Kendermore Cobbler|HFFotM}. While the Kender themselves often get (unfairly) pegged as sneaks and thieves, there's nothing shady about their food and flavors.

Of course, rogues are creatures of shadow, so it follows that they populate not only every corner of the Material Plane, but its echo planes also. While there's little pleasure to be found in the dismal Shadowfell, the wandering rogues who brave its gray terrain will tell you that the {@recipe Tavern Crickets|HFFotM} and {@recipe Honey milk|HFFotM} make it bearable enough to stay. On the other side of the divide, in the Feywild, mischievous eladrin rogues lose their inhibitions entirely at the sight of a bowl of {@recipe Seelie Court Cheese and Potato Soup|HFFotM}, especially when paired with a decanter of rare {@recipe Elverquisst|HFFotM}. Rogues fleeing retribution or the law via the planes might palm a {@recipe Chirper's Sugar Biscuits|HFFotM|Chirper's Sugar Biscuit} while visiting the Market District of Sigil or a {@recipe Vada's Vanilla Buns|HFFotM|Vanilla Bun} from Vada's Otherworldly Goods in the Dancing Night Market.

entries.name: Stealing Bites
entries: Wise adventurers know that having a rogue on board always means fuller purses and fuller bellies. When it comes to rogue cuisine itself, there are really only two types: The kind you survive {@i on} and the kind you survive {@i for}. The perennially on-the-run rogue will always endure the former so they can enjoy the latter.

entries.title: "I am he who rules the world, don't you know? One little piece at a time."–Jarlaxle

data.name: Sorcerer

entries: Darling, how can I pick a favorite when I haven't tried everything yet?

Magic is a science to be studied for some, but for {@class Sorcerer|XPHB|sorcerers}, it is intuition. Raw, wild power waits below the surface to be unlocked and released by the sorcerer's sheer will. Whether the sorcerer feels it to be a gift or a curse, their magic is an essential part of them. The life of a sorcerer is thus a delicate balancing act, channeling the magic within them without ever taming it, mustering the discipline to harness it without letting it consume them. A sorcerer grows by improvising, gradually discovering new facets of their gift sometimes through incremental improvements and sometimes in spectacular breakthroughs. Any chance experience might prove the key to a deeper understanding of themselves—and food is the source of the most primordial of experiences.

entries.name: Side Effects
entries: The self-experimentation so essential to the development of sorcerous magic necessarily involves diet. Some sorcerers may fast for prolonged periods or eat only at odd and irregular hours. Just as some half-forgotten taste or smell can cause childhood memories to flood back, an unexpected combination of flavors might connect deeply with a sorcerer.

Not everyone can be a sorcerer, but a sorcerer can come from any background. As such, the table manners of a sorcerer range from refined to rustic. Some sorcerers are perfectly at home in the finest dining establishments; others are more comfortable in a lowly tavern or a sedate meadow. But then there's always one who takes their tea underwater and upside down. Sorcerers are rare, and as their source of power is within themselves, they can be introverted and solitary. Whether you join a sorcerer for a meal around a king's table or a campfire, you may find it hard to share a menu with them.

entries.name: Expect the Unexpected
entries: Sorcerers may be subject to inexplicable cravings for esoteric ingredients. Out of a desire to overcome their limitations, sorcerers will challenge themselves with food they find distasteful or ingredients that might not strictly be considered edible. A sorcerer might even undertake a quest for the sole purpose of sourcing a rare meat or vegetable or spice—whatever it takes to achieve total self-actualization.

The supernatural side effects that afflict sorcerers may also alter their dining habits, resulting in quirks ranging from minor eccentricities to dramatic shifts in how—and what—a sorcerer might eat. Thus, inviting a sorcerer over to dinner might present some challenges. You might be embarrassed to learn that they suddenly don't eat anything red—and flummoxed when, the week after, they now don't eat anything that is not red. Whatever you put on a sorcerer's plate, you may observe that a bit of {@spell prestidigitation|XPHB} has converted it into something else entirely before it goes down the hatch. Sorcerers have a fondness for modifying foods with magic in no small part because some happy accident may lead to an unexpected but quite delicious outcome.

Much of a sorcerer's demeanor and appetite depends on the source of their innate power. Sorcerers whose magic derives from a {@subclass Draconic|Sorcerer|XPHB|XPHB|draconic bloodline} may try to align their diet with that of their forbears, which varies, of course, by dragon color but very likely involves copious amounts of fresh meat or anything that goes well with {@recipe Dragonfire Mead|HFLotT}. {@subclass Aberrant|Sorcerer|XPHB|XPHB|Aberrant sorcerers} may hunger for things eaten on other planes, places where living humanoids were never meant to set foot, where every bite can be its own perilous adventure. {@subclass Clockwork|Sorcerer|XPHB|XPHB|Clockwork sorcerers} delight in precision and in especially well-timed and judiciously executed meals. And for sorcerers of pure {@subclass wild magic|Sorcerer|XPHB|XPHB}, anything goes—maybe those iridescent butterflies you just created will turn out to be the most delicious dessert garnish in the world!

entries.name: Worlds of Possibility
entries: Sorcerers are some of the most traveled of adventurers; powerful sorcerers are known to pass among worlds extensively. Not all realms look kindly on practitioners of wild magic, preferring the traditional scholarly wizards of yore. But everywhere sorcerers roam, they can be assured of new mysteries to unlock and new cuisines to enjoy.

Faerûn's sorcerers draw on the raw magic of the Weave, forsaking the intercessors and patrons favored by more conservative spellcasters. The wild magic thus unleashed can be unpredictable, but Faerûn is home to meta-magicians adept at fixing spells on the fly. The most powerful of these sorcerers have developed quite rarefied tastes, traveling far and wide to take in all manner of exotic dishes. The mad sorcerer Emirikol, a famous planeswalker often residing in Faerûn, is said to favor {@recipe Otyugh Steak|HFLotT|Otyugh Steaks}, a delicacy shunned in his home world of Greyhawk.

Krynn is one of several realms that acknowledges sorcery as the most ancient and primal form of magic. The Academy of Sorcery, near the town of Solace, offered tutelage for a time not far from the Inn of the Last Home. Orders like the Legion of Steel are known to employ sorcerers in their campaigns. Many sorcerers in Krynn favor the meditative power of {@recipe Par-Salian's Tea|HF} to turn the mind inward in search of fresh discoveries.

Sorcerers stray to far stranger realms. They may enjoy a {@recipe Sensate Palate Cleanser|HFFotM} while visiting Sigil before they embark on culinary adventures unavailable anywhere else in the multiverse. The sorcerous scholars of Strixhaven indulge in {@recipe Black Lotus Root|HFFotM}. On Eberron, a jaded palate might seek out the dishes made with sparkle mushrooms at the Celestial Vista, like the golden pheasant—full of flavors that would make anyone feel like a favored soul. Even in Avernus there might be a delicacy or two to be found, like {@recipe Candied Phase Spider Eyes|HFLotT}.

entries.name: Adventures in Sensation
entries: There is perhaps no greater culinary adventurer than a sorcerer. But they may not be much for recipes, just as they have no use for spellbooks—to make an experience repeatable seems almost anathema to a sorcerer. But you do need some way to keep track of which exact dishes you've tried and how they might be spiced up. What might inspire nothing but diffidence in one sorcerer might electrify another.

data.name: Warlock

entries: I wouldn't think of eating something that I couldn't share with her.

True power comes with a price, and {@class Warlock|XPHB|warlocks} are those who dare pay it. They alone pursue the secret rites that bind them to a patron, a relationship that becomes the font of both wisdom and magic. The pact they forge can take many forms, ranging from apprenticeship to subservience to worship. Patronage is a form of companionship but an unbalanced one: Warlocks are never alone, and someone is always looking over their shoulder. The pact with their patron suffuses every aspect of a warlock's life, including their relationship with food. Some patrons may favor banquets and lavish cuisines; others may encourage temperance or even self-abnegation. A warlock may well find that fare disliked by their patron turns to ashes in their mouth.

entries.name: Bound to Their Appetites
entries: Contrary to popular belief, not all warlocks are thralls to demons, trading their souls away on the installment plan for scraps of magic and power. But no patron extends gifts to a warlock without expecting something in return. Many warlocks believe they have the upper hand in this exchange, that they are on a path to being the true masters. But warlocks act in the world on behalf of their patrons, knowingly or unknowingly; in some perhaps mysterious way, warlocks further their patrons' goals.

It requires a keen analytical mind to discern the very mysteries of the multiverse and a bold spirit to grasp for the hand by which those mysteries were written. Warlocks can be justifiably proud of what they have achieved, and with that may come a certain entitlement. Almost anything could be to a warlock's palate provided it is an elevated dish, something that has earned its place on the table. Some might mistake the refined tastes of a warlock for snobbery, but for all that, warlocks tend to be pleasant dining companions, charming if sometimes supercilious.

As warlocks understand the transactional nature of sacrifice, few among them are vegetarians. Some things must die to fuel the power of others. But a warlock would be unlikely to squander magic for the sake of being fed; warlocks are of a higher station in life than that.

entries.name: Me, Myself, and You
entries: For all their pride in their accomplishments, some warlocks may be accused of taking shortcuts—their path to power is not based on wizardly book learning or sorcerous inspiration but instead on a sort of deal with the devil. As such, warlocks may not always prove the most fastidious of chefs. They tend to be more interested in eating food than in preparing it. If someone cannot be paid to do the cooking, then perhaps someone—or something—can be compelled or summoned to do it.

Much of a warlock's attitude toward food will vary with the nature of their pact. Warlocks with a {@subclass Archfey|Warlock|XPHB|XPHB|fey patron} may be given to banqueting and indulgence at the table, more for the joy of hedonism than to satiate hunger or thirst. The most austere of warlocks form a bond with a {@subclass Celestial|Warlock|XPHB|XPHB|celestial}, who would encourage—if not demand—austerity and temperance. Those who contract with a {@subclass Fiend|Warlock|XPHB|XPHB|fiend} might nervously play at the bon vivant as whispers from the pit encourage them to commit blasphemies and atrocities. Who dares imagine the eldritch fare that a warlock pledged to the {@subclass Great Old One|Warlock|XPHB|XPHB|Great Old Ones} might be forced to endure? Dining with such a patron might involve a shadowy proboscis implanting a sinister egg deep in a warlock's guts, where it will lie dormant...for now.

Those warlocks who keep a familiar might share a meal with it, as the patron's surrogate at the warlock's side—though maybe not if the familiar is a {@creature skeleton|XMM}. But in the company of other mortal diners, a warlock is happy to share their bounty and their company.

entries.name: Planar Pairings
entries: The bond between a warlock and a patron varies in the different realms of the multiverse. In some places where patrons are basically deities, it can be hard to distinguish warlocks from clerics. The eldritch powers of the outer planes could never channel divine magic; yet they can still bestow power on those reckless enough to seek it from them. But because these bonds span planes, warlocks across the multiverse have more in common than other sorts of magic users do: From the perspective of their patrons, all warlocks are drawn from basically the same talent pool.

Fiend patrons are perhaps the most common across the worlds, and their tastes would encourage any warlock to indulge in fare like {@recipe Fried Fingers|HF}. The Abyss and the Nine Hells are indeed places that warlocks are not unlikely to visit over the course of their careers, as when Ammon Jerro found his patron {@creature Levistus|CoA}. A warlock from Faerûn who sits down to a dinner in Avernus with their patron may find a dish like {@recipe Abyssal Chicken Egg Omelet|HFLotT} appeals to both, in different ways.

Greyhawk is unusual in that many potential patrons for warlocks are demigods who still tread the Oerth. The warlocks of Greyhawk might pledge themselves to {@deity Iuz|Greyhawk|XDMG}, the demonic namesake of a huge northerly region known for its blasted terrain. They're likely to find fare at the numerous taverns outside Iuz's confines. Only the most crazed practitioners of forbidden lore in Greyhawk would dare pledge themselves to the inscrutable likes of {@deity Tharizdun|Greyhawk|XDMG}, but those who do might develop an inexplicable craving for {@recipe Pickled Vine Blight Salad|HFLotT}.

entries.name: Just the Two of Us
entries: Only those who've sworn themselves to a patron can truly understand that bond. It is both a push and a pull, a desire to comply and to resist, a source of power, and at the same time, a vulnerable dependence. Whether warlocks seek to emulate their patrons or to counter them, their patron's nature looms over how they comport themselves, how they dress, and how they eat. That is, right up until they have enough power to throw off this yoke—then they'll truly be their own master.

entries: {@class Wizard|XPHB|Wizards} are the consummate scholars of magic, dedicating their lives to the study of ancient tomes and the manipulation of the Weave, the unseen cosmic lattice that governs all magical forces. These arcane academics often lead lives of rigorous study, obsessive experimentation, and the occasional jaunt through other planes of existence in their relentless pursuit of knowledge.

entries.name: Arcane Appetites
entries: With their mastery of components (a spell's fundamental ingredients) and their deep respect for arcane "recipes," wizards often approach magic much like the culinary arts. In fact, wizardry and cooking share more than a few parallels: Both require precision, creativity, and an eye for transformation. A wizard's cuisine is an alchemical blend of pragmatism, arcane flair, and imaginative innovation. Their tastes range from the esoteric and extravagant to the ascetic and efficient, shaped by personality, resources, and realm of origin.

Across the multiverse, wizards enchant their meals to enhance flavor, preserve freshness, or even grant restorative magic. A wizard's larder often rivals their component pouch, fully stocked with rare herbs, planar spices, and magically cultivated produce. Some dishes may feature simple fare elevated with a magical twist; others may be wholly otherworldly creations.

entries.name: Culinary Conjurers
entries: Some wizards are so consumed by study that they barely have time for mundane activities such as cooking. They prefer efficient meals with minimal mess, allowing them to return quickly to their spellcraft. These repasts might be prepared by their {@spell unseen servant|XPHB} while their master works late into the night. Other wizards, however, embrace cooking with the same enthusiasm they bring to their spellcraft, often delighting in the challenge, the parallels, and the possibilities. To these culinary conjurers, the kitchen is just another kind of laboratory.

{@spell Simulacrum|XPHB} sous-chefs may assist in the preparation, and the fire used to cook may even be magically mustered, sometimes adding an extra elemental touch to the dish. However, while many wizards employ magic to streamline the process, like cutting a roast's cook time from hours to minutes, others shun shortcuts in favor of the joy of creation. Magic items like the {@item cauldron of plenty|IDRotF} can ingeniously transform water into a nourishing stew from thin air, but such "culinary cheats" can lack the artistry that many wizards crave.

Presentation matters, especially for wizards who often pride themselves on their {@spell prestidigitation|XPHB} prowess. An {@subclass Illusionist|Wizard|XPHB|XPHB} wizard may add an extra level of flamboyance to the experience, making platters levitate or illusionary garnishes shimmer. If an ingredient is missing, a resourceful {@subclass Conjurer|Wizard|XPHB|AU} wizard might simply summon it on the spot. An {@subclass Abjurer|Wizard|XPHB|XPHB|Abjuration} wizard may imbue a meal with added protections to ward off certain evils, while a {@subclass Diviner|Wizard|XPHB|XPHB} might seek to add an incantation that imbues their meals with ability to part the veil of space, time, and consciousness. The wizard makes for a most creative and resourceful chef.

entries.name: A Taste of the Planes
entries: One thing is certain: Wizard food is as unpredictable as the wizards themselves. Their culinary preferences vary wildly across cultures, traditions, and realms.

On Krynn, wizardly diets often reflect the ethos of the {@background Mage of High Sorcery|DSotDQ|Orders of High Sorcery}. At the Tower of High Sorcery in Wayreth, {@feat Adept of the White Robes|DSotDQ|White Robes}, {@feat Adept of the Red Robes|DSotDQ|Red Robes}, and {@feat Adept of the Black Robes|DSotDQ|Black Robes} alike dine on austere meals, simple stews, bread, and tea, echoing their disciplined lives. {@recipe Dragon Salmon|HF}, plated with a red wine reduction, offers up an intelligent protein. But there are also rare delicacies like Moonroot Soup, harvested under the light of Solinari, said to enhance mental clarity. {@feat Adept of the Black Robes|DSotDQ|Black Robes}, favoring indulgence, may enjoy rich, preserved meats and Bloodberry Wine that symbolize power.

At Strixhaven University, a venerated school of magic on the Plane of Arcavios, the food is as intellectually stimulating as the curriculum. In the Biblioplex Café, the university's central dining hub, the menu changes daily, driven by the chef's whims. Students snack on Mystery Memory Muffins that sharpen their recall of lessons, while fun finds its way onto the plate as well—Prismari Edible Art that melts like chocolate sculptures and Quandrix Fractal Sandwiches that unfold in perfect geometry with every bite.

On Faerûn, in places of arcane study such as Candlekeep, a revered fortress-library perched on the Sword Coast, meals range from practical to posh. Within its cloistered walls, notable eateries cater to the magically inclined. The Hearth is a dining hall–style establishment that serves comfort food capable of arcane replenishment, including Scholar's Stew, a thick lamb and root vegetable medley seasoned with rosemary that is known to stimulate memory. In the House of Rest, a visiting scholar could cap their day with a refreshing {@recipe Ray of Frost|HFFotM}, a cerulean concoction to relax the mind. Further north in Waterdeep's Blackstaff Tower, which serves as both a magical stronghold and training ground, elite mages might find themselves fortunate to indulge on Blackstaff's Delight, a rare dessert reserved for special occasions. This dark chocolate torte, accented with a hint of cayenne and embellished with an edible silver leaf, is said to not only ensorcel one's taste buds but to have been dreamed up by Khelben "Blackstaff" Arunsun himself.

In the arcane-abundant societies of the planet Eberron, culinary magic is practically institutionalized with advanced preparation techniques often enlivening classic concepts. Here, magically concocted cuisine is commonplace, including {@recipe Cremfels|HFLotT}, an infectiously delicious dessert served to over-studied magicians of Morgrave University. Magewrights even specialize in gastronomic magic, preparing meals that restore spell-casting capabilities or calm wild surges such as Soothebrew Tea.

In Sigil, the nexus of the known multiverse, food becomes an interplanar experience. Here, wizard chefs reign supreme in a fusion of cultures and cuisines. With portals to countless realms, ingredients in this planar melting pot range from the mundane to the mystically dangerous. This extraordinary city is a haven for mages in search of rare components and for chefs seeking new frontiers...and frequently, they are one and the same as exemplified in the refined flavors of a serving of Silverquill {@recipe Squid Ink Pasta with Scallops|HFLotT}. Similarly, The Styx Oarsman tavern, situated in the Lower Ward of Sigil, may be notorious for shady dealings, but its Ethereal Soufflé, said to rise under the guidance of a wizard's hand, is equally legendary.

entries.name: Table for One...Thousand Realms
entries: Across the multiverse, wizards command staggering arcane power, but their culinary tastes are just as varied and captivating as their spellbooks. Discerning and often whimsical, a wizard's palate favors subtle twists on the familiar, where creativity and thoughtful experimentation are highly prized. Whether practical or performative, austere or extravagant, wizardly cuisine reveals a universal truth: Even the most brilliant minds need to eat, and when they do, they often bring a little magic to the table.

data.name: Afterword: The Adventure Continues
entries: Every quest ends with a meal—a moment to rest, reflect, and raise a tankard with your companions. As we close out this chapter of {@i Heroes' Feast}, we invite you to do just that. Whether you found inspiration in a ranger's fireside skillet, a wizard's arcane elixir, or a rogue's late-night indulgence, we hope these class-inspired recipes brought the Dungeons & Dragons experience a little closer to your table and taste buds.

With this book, {@book Heroes' Feast: Legends of the Table|HFLotT}, we set out to explore the culinary traditions, personalities, and storytelling potential of D&D's iconic classes—from the stoic discipline of paladins to the wild-hearted creativity of bards. Each recipe was designed not just to nourish but to echo the spirit of its class. We aimed to capture the humor, heart, and heritage of what it means to live and eat like a true adventurer.

This tome joins a growing compendium of {@i Heroes' Feast} creations: the original {@book Heroes' Feast|HF}, a culinary foundation inspired by the peoples of D&D; {@book Heroes' Feast: Flavors of the Multiverse|HFFotM}, which includes recipes that traverse the planes and explore D&D's many worlds; {@deck Deck of Many Morsels|HFDoMM|The Deck of Many Morsels}, a flavorful foray into snacks and sweets; and twenty hourlong episodes of {@link Heroes' Feast|https://www.imdb.com/title/tt29624051/}, the official D&D cooking show, which brought many of these dishes to life one bite at a time. Together, these projects have built something bigger than any one book—a shared table for fans, families, game nights, and hungry heroes across the realms.

Whether you're a seasoned adventurer or a newly initiated cook, we hope this book offered something meaningful: a moment of creativity, a new technique, or just a reason to gather with your fellowship. The campaign may be over, but the feast goes on. And with a bit of imagination and a dash of courage, the next great meal is never far away.
Until then, may your pans stay hot, your parties stay full, and remember: {@i Never split the party—host the party!}
We shall see you at the next table.

data.name: Acknowledgments
entries: As lifelong D&D players and participants, we are forever grateful to all those who dreamt, built, and expanded upon this remarkable game—a wellspring of imagination, camaraderie, and inspiration that has shaped so much of our lives. D&D has given each of us more than we could ever repay, and not a day goes by that we don't marvel at the fact that we get to contribute to its storied legacy. The {@i Heroes' Feast} franchise, in particular, has been an unexpected and extraordinary gift—one that continues to fill us with a profound sense of honor, gratitude, and sense of privilege to be a part of its ever-growing adventure.

When it comes to projects like this, no one can go it alone. True success demands the talents, dedication, and collaboration of a team of skilled professionals—a well-balanced party, if you will. You might even say it's like a real-life D&D campaign.

Our list of thanks is far too long to be confined within these pages, but we'll do our best to scratch the surface. Firstly, thank you to our families and friends, who are our everlasting fount of love, support, and inspiration. Next, to the people and organizations that made this book possible, specifically Ten Speed Press, Wizards of the Coast, publisher Aaron Wehner (who originated the idea of a D&D cookbook!), D&D publishing lead Paul Morrissey, master chef Adam Ried, editors Claire Yee and Shaida Boroumand, creative director Kelly Booth, production editor Joyce Wong, production designer Mari Gill, production manager Kelli Tokos, marketer Paola Crespo, publicist Maya Bradford, illustrator Goodname, photographer Ray Kachatorian, food stylist Amanda Anselmino, and prop stylist Glenn Jenkins. Thank you also to our late agent and friend Jacques de Spoelberch, a veritable wizard of a man who would have so enjoyed seeing the pages herein. Last, but not least, thank you to you, the fans who truly make the game and the food what it is.

The Dungeons & Dragons experts behind the bestselling {@book Heroes' Feast|HF} and {@book Heroes' Feast: Flavors of the Multiverse|HFFotM} explores the tastes and delights of each playable class, introducing you to the culinary traditions of druids, bards, sorcerers, and more. Eighty recipes are pulled from beloved inns, magical colleges, deadly dungeons, and other iconic locales that span the realms. Each recipe, developed by a professional chef from one of America's top test kitchens, is delicious, easy to prepare, and composed of ingredients readily found in our world. With recipes like {@recipe Flash-Fried Berry Fritters|HFLotT}, {@recipe River Fish Fry|HFLotT}, {@recipe Wren Pot Pie|HFLotT}, and {@recipe Dragonfire Mead|HFLotT}, your next campaign is bound to be the ultimate success.
